**Crowley** (Local pronunciation: [/ˈ k r æ l i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")) is a city in, and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of, [Acadia Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadia_Parish,_Louisiana "Acadia Parish, Louisiana") in the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Crowley had a population of 11,710.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-4) Crowley is the principal city of the Crowley [micropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropolitan_statistical_area "Micropolitan statistical area"), which includes all of Acadia Parish. It is also part of the larger [Lafayette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafayette,_Louisiana "Lafayette, Louisiana")–[Acadiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadiana "Acadiana")[combined statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafayette-Acadiana_combined_statistical_area "Lafayette-Acadiana combined statistical area").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crowley,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Crowley was founded in 1886 by brothers [C.C. "Curley" Duson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curley_Duson "Curley Duson") and W.W. Duson. Curley Duson was sheriff of [St. Landry Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Landry_Parish,_Louisiana "St. Landry Parish, Louisiana"), of which the Crowley townsite was then a part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-5) Incorporated in 1887, W.W. Duson, General Manager of Southwest Louisiana Land Company, plotted and developed Crowley. W.W. Duson's daughter, Maime Duson, married Percy Lee Lawrence, who founded the First National Bank of Crowley. The 7-story building was once the tallest building between [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston") and [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans").

The town was named after Patrick E. Crowley (1850-1909), an Irish-born employee of the [Louisiana Western Rail Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Western_Rail_Road?action=edit&redlink=1 "Louisiana Western Rail Road (page does not exist)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-7) Crowley was in charge of a small facility nicknamed "Crowley's Switch" near [Estherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estherwood,_Louisiana "Estherwood, Louisiana"). The Dusons persuaded Crowley to move the switch about seven miles east to the Dusons' land in exchange for naming the town for him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-8)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crowley,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 5.85 square miles (15.2 km 2), all land.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-9)

[Louisiana Highway 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Highway_13 "Louisiana Highway 13") passes through the city with [Kaplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaplan,_Louisiana "Kaplan, Louisiana"), which is located in [Vermilion Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermilion_Parish,_Louisiana "Vermilion Parish, Louisiana"), being located 19 miles southeast and [Eunice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunice,_Louisiana "Eunice, Louisiana"), located in both [Acadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadia_Parish "Acadia Parish") and [St. Landry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Landry_Parish "St. Landry Parish")[parishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County "County"), is located 20 miles north. The city of [Rayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayne,_Louisiana "Rayne, Louisiana") is located 9 miles east of Crowley via [U.S. Highway 90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_90 "U.S. Route 90") and [I-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_10 "Interstate 10"). The city of [Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennings,_Louisiana "Jennings, Louisiana") is located 17 miles west via [U.S. Highway 90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_90 "U.S. Route 90") and [I-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_10 "Interstate 10").

At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), there were 11,710 people, 4,807 households, and 2,934 families residing in the city. At the 2019 [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey"), there were 4,807 households.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-:0-16)

In 2019, the racial and ethnic makeup of the city was 58.5% [non-Hispanic or Latino white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Hispanic_or_Latino_whites "Non-Hispanic or Latino whites"), 34.8% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans"), <0.0% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), 0.4% some other race, 1.9% [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"), and 4.4% [Hispanic and Latin American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") of any race.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-17) At the [2000 U.S. census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"), the racial and ethic makeup was 67.83% [White American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), 30.98% Black or African American, 0.15% [American Indian and Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 0.29% Asian, 0.01% [Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") or [other Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_Americans "Pacific Islander Americans"), 0.23% from other races, and 0.51% from two or more races. Hispanics and Latin Americans were 1.10% of the population.

There were 4,807 households, and 33.5% were married couples living together, 18.5% male households with no female present, and 41.8% female households with no male present.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-:0-16) The average family size was 3.34.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 5.4% aged 5 and under, 72.4% aged 18 and older, and 17.2% aged 65 and older. The median age was 37.7 years, up from 35 years at the 2000 United States census.

The median income for a household in the city was $26,972. Family households had a median income of $31,168, married couples had a median income of $50,066, and non-family households had a median income of $19,138. An estimated 37.1% of the population lived at or below the poverty line.

## Arts and culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crowley,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arts and culture")]

Crowley is noted for its annual [International Rice Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Rice_Festival "International Rice Festival").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-18) Crowley has the nickname of "Rice Capital of the World",[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-20) because at one time it was a major center for rice harvesting and milling. Today, Crowley still has a number of rice mills and rice is the main crop of many local farmers.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crowley,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

The [Crowley High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley_High_School_(Louisiana) "Crowley High School (Louisiana)") "Fighting Gents" were State Division 3A champions in the 1989 football season and had an 8–2 regular season.

Crowley is also the home of [Notre Dame High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_High_School_(Crowley,_Louisiana) "Notre Dame High School (Crowley, Louisiana)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-21) Notre Dame is an Acadia Parish-wide [Catholic high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_high_school "Catholic high school") whose football program has won six state championships and numerous District Champion titles, in addition to numerous state championships in other sports, such as men's baseball, women's softball, men's tennis, men's track & field, and women's volleyball.

**Oberlin** is a town in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [Allen Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish,_Louisiana "Allen Parish, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Oberlin had a population of 1,402.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-4) The town is named after [Johann Friedrich Oberlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Friedrich_Oberlin "Johann Friedrich Oberlin").

Oberlin was the home of Ernest S. Clements, a [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") member of the [Louisiana State Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") and, later, the [Louisiana Public Service Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Public_Service_Commission "Louisiana Public Service Commission"). He ran unsuccessfully in 1944 for [governor of Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Louisiana "Governor of Louisiana").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 4.4 square miles (11.4 km 2), all land.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census_2010-5) Oberlin is located on [U.S. Route 165](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_165 "U.S. Route 165") at [LA 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Highway_26 "Louisiana Highway 26").

As of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), there were 1,402 people, 496 households, and 313 families residing in the town.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-12) of 2000, there were 1,853 people, 702 households, and 464 families residing in the town. The population density was 602.0 inhabitants per square mile (232.4/km 2). There were 789 housing units at an average density of 256.3 per square mile (99.0/km 2).

The racial makeup of the town was 60.28% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 37.61% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.76% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.27% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.16% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.92% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 0.70% of the population.

There were 702 households, out of which 34.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 45.0% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 17.7% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.8% were non-families. 31.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.43 and the average family size was 3.06.

In the town, the population was spread out, with 26.4% under the age of 18, 8.0% from 18 to 24, 25.1% from 25 to 44, 24.5% from 45 to 64, and 16.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 38 years. For every 100 females, there were 90.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 83.8 males.

The median income for a household in the town was $23,333, and the median income for a family was $30,583. Males had a median income of $28,558 versus $16,923 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the town was $12,050. About 18.3% of families and 25.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 30.3% of those under age 18 and 31.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

[Allen Parish School Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish_School_Board "Allen Parish School Board") operates [Oberlin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin_High_School_(Louisiana) "Oberlin High School (Louisiana)") and Oberlin Elementary School in Oberlin.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-13)

There is a private school, Oberlin Covenant School, which opened circa 1986. In 1992, two people worked to operate the school, and there were five teachers who worked full time. That year, its enrollment was 40, and there were six students per teacher, a ratio lower than those of public schools.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-14)

**Marksville** is a small city in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [Avoyelles Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avoyelles_Parish,_Louisiana "Avoyelles Parish, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Marksville had a population of 5,065.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-4)

Louisiana's first land-based [casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino "Casino"), Paragon Casino Resort, opened in Marksville in June 1994. It is operated by the federally recognized [Tunica-Biloxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunica-Biloxi "Tunica-Biloxi") Indian Tribe, which has a reservation in the parish.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marksville,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Marksville_District.jpg/250px-Marksville_District.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marksville_District.jpg)

[Marksville Commercial Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville_Commercial_Historic_District "Marksville Commercial Historic District")

The land where Marksville was founded on was once a meeting place, leading to the present day [Marksville Prehistoric Indian Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville_Prehistoric_Indian_Site "Marksville Prehistoric Indian Site").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)

Marksville is named after Marc Eliche (Marco Litche or Marco de Élitxe, as recorded by the Spanish), a [Sephardic Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardic_Jews "Sephardic Jews") trader believed to be from [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice"), who established a [trading post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trading_post "Trading post") after his wagon broke down in this area.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-Leeper2012-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-9) His Italian name was recorded by a Spanish priest as _Marco Litche;_ French priests, who were with colonists, recorded his name as _Marc Eliche_ or _Mark Eliché_[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-:0-10) after his trading post was established about 1794. Marksville was noted on Louisiana maps as early as 1809, after the United States acquired the territory in the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase") of 1803.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-:0-10) Eliche later donated the land that became the Courthouse Square in the center of Marksville.

Marksville's population has numerous families of [Anglo Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglo_Americans "Anglo Americans") ancestry, in addition to African Americans, European Americans, and persons of mixed European-African ancestry. Many of the families had ancestors here since the city was incorporated.

Marksville became the trading center of a rural area developed as cotton [plantations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantations_in_the_American_South "Plantations in the American South"). After the United States outlawed the Atlantic slave trade in 1808, enslavers purchased [African-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American "African-American")[slaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") through the domestic [slave trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_slavery "History of slavery"); a total of more than one million were transported to the [Deep South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_South "Deep South") from the [Upper South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_South "Upper South") in the first half of the 19th century. Enslavers typically bought slaves from markets in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), where they had been taken via the Mississippi River or by the coastal slave trade at sea. [Solomon Northup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_Northup "Solomon Northup"), a [free black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Negro "Free Negro") man from [Saratoga Springs, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saratoga_Springs,_New_York "Saratoga Springs, New York"), was kidnapped and sold into slavery in Louisiana. After being held for nearly 12 years on plantations in Avoyelles Parish, he was freed in 1853 with the help of Marksville and New York officials. Northup's memoir, which he published after returning to New York, was the basis of the 2013 movie _[12 Years A Slave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Years\_A\_Slave\_(film) "12 Years A Slave (film)")_, of the same name. On January 4, 2026 (the 173rd anniversary of his release from slavery), _Hope Out of Darkness_, a bronze statue of Northup created by American sculptor [Wesley Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Wofford?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wesley Wofford (page does not exist)"), will be unveiled in Marksville. Commissioned by the Solomon Northup Committee for Commemorative Works, the sculpture depicts Northup breaking free from chains with papers (his narrative) as a torch, symbolizing freedom and resilience.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-11)

### 1947 Rain of Fish Incident

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marksville,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1947 Rain of Fish Incident")]

On October 23, 1947, between seven and eight o’clock in the morning, hundreds fish ranging from two to nine inches in length [fell from the sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_of_animals "Rain of animals") onto the streets and yards of Marksville.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-Science-12) These were local freshwater fish, including: Large-mouth black bass ([Micropterus salmoides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropterus_salmoides "Micropterus salmoides")), goggle-eye ([Lepomis gulosus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepomis_gulosus "Lepomis gulosus")), several species of minnows, and hickory shad ([Alosa mediocris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alosa_mediocris "Alosa mediocris")).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-Science-12)

All primary public schools are run by the [Avoyelles Parish School Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avoyelles_Parish_School_Board "Avoyelles Parish School Board"), which operates two schools within the city of Marksville.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-17) In January 2018, 5 children from Marksville died in a car accident while traveling through [Gainesville, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gainesville,_Florida "Gainesville, Florida").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-Santana_2018-18)

*   [Chester Coco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Coco "Chester Coco") (1915–2001), lawyer and Louisiana state senator[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marksville,_Louisiana#cite_note-:02-22)

*   [Tommy Neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Neck "Tommy Neck"), LSU and NFL football player from the 1960s
*   [Ed Oliver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Oliver_(American_football) "Ed Oliver (American football)"), [NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL "NFL") football player
*   [John H. Overton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Overton "John H. Overton") (1875–1948), U.S. senator, native of Marksville

**Arcadia** is a town in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [Bienville Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bienville_Parish,_Louisiana "Bienville Parish, Louisiana") in northern [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Arcadia had a population of 2,746.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-5) Arcadia has the highest elevation of any incorporated municipality in Louisiana. Arcadia's name commemorates the Ancient Greek region of [Arcadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia_(ancient_region) "Arcadia (ancient region)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1934, bank robbers [Bonnie and Clyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde "Bonnie and Clyde") were killed near Arcadia in a shootout. Their bodies were brought for embalming to a furniture store in Arcadia which also served as a funeral parlor. Enormous crowds of onlookers descended upon the city when news of the pair's deaths there became public.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-8)

Arcadia has been a center of the poultry industry, with up to 300 independent growers for years supplying the local feed mill operated by poultry company [Pilgrim's Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilgrim's_Pride "Pilgrim's Pride").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 2009 the company, facing bankruptcy, announced that it would close most of its Louisiana operations, including plants in Arcadia, [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Louisiana "Athens, Louisiana"), [Choudrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choudrant,_Louisiana "Choudrant, Louisiana"), and [Farmerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmerville,_Louisiana "Farmerville, Louisiana"); these operations were estimated to have provided a combined 1,300 jobs.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-pilpr-9) Several weeks later, Pilgrim's Pride accepted a [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")80 million (equivalent to $120 million in 2025) offer from [Foster Farms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_Farms_(poultry_company) "Foster Farms (poultry company)") of California to purchase their operations and keep the plants running. Foster Farms put up $40 million of the purchase price, with the other $40 million covered by the State of Louisiana.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-10)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 3.1 square miles (7.9 km 2), all land.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census_2010-11) It is 50 miles (80 km) east of [Shreveport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreveport,_Louisiana "Shreveport, Louisiana").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-12)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Arcadia had a population of 2,746. The median age was 42.5 years. 21.3% of residents were under the age of 18 and 21.8% were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females, there were 79.7 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 75.9 males.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PL-16)

0.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DHC-17)

There were 1,124 households in Arcadia, including 620 families. Of all households, 28.1% had children under the age of 18 living in them. 24.5% were married-couple households, 20.1% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 50.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 37.6% of all households were made up of individuals, and 15.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. There were 1,321 housing units, of which 14.9% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 6.2%.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-15)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

At the census of 2000,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-18) there were 3,041 people, 1,071 households, and 737 families residing in the town. The population density was 1,025.6 inhabitants per square mile (396.0/km 2). There were 1,231 housing units at an average density of 415.2 units per square mile (160.3 units/km 2).

The racial makeup of the town was 37.98% White, 60.57% African American, 0.26% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 0.10% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), 0.26% from [various other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.82% from multiple or mixed races. [Hispanics or Latinos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") of any race were 1.61% of the population.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-18)

In 2000, there were 1,071 households, out of which 31.7% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 37.0% were married couples living together, 27.9% had a female householder with no husband present, and 31.1% were non-families. 28.5% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.7% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.57 and the average family size was 3.16. In the town of Arcadia, the population was spread out, with 27.1% under the age of 18, 9.2% from 18 to 24, 24.4% from 25 to 44, 18.7% from 45 to 64, and 20.6% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 81.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 73.3 males.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-18)

### Income and poverty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Income and poverty")]

The median income for a household in the town was $21,661, and the median income for a family was $26,250. Males had a median income of $25,885 versus $17,279 for females. The per capita income for the town was $10,962. About 27.1% of families and 31.4% of the population were below the poverty line, including 42.7% of those under age 18 and 20.6% of those age 65 or over.

At the 2019 census estimates, the median household income increased to $23,494. About 41.9% of the population lived at or below the poverty line, and 17.5% of Arcadia's citizens held a bachelor's degree or higher.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-:0-19)

### Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Religion")]

Among the numerous churches in downtown Arcadia are First [United Methodist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church") and the First [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist "Baptist") Church, both in large sanctuaries. The [Louisiana Baptist Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Baptist_Convention "Louisiana Baptist Convention") was founded in 1848 in nearby [Mount Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lebanon,_Louisiana "Mount Lebanon, Louisiana"), south of [Gibsland, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibsland,_Louisiana "Gibsland, Louisiana").

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Government")]

The Bienville Parish Courthouse was formerly located in a residential section of Arcadia but moved in 2013 to a newly constructed building off [Interstate 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_20 "Interstate 20").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-20)

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Media")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Bienville_Democrat_newspaper%2C_Arcadia%2C_LA_IMG_0808.JPG/250px-Bienville_Democrat_newspaper%2C_Arcadia%2C_LA_IMG_0808.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bienville_Democrat_newspaper,_Arcadia,_LA_IMG_0808.JPG)

The _Bienville Democrat_ office in Arcadia

The weekly newspaper, _The Bienville Democrat_, is printed on Wednesdays in [Natchitoches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natchitoches,_Louisiana "Natchitoches, Louisiana"), and then distributed across Bienville Parish.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

Public schools within Arcadia are under the jurisdiction of the [Bienville Parish School Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bienville_Parish_School_Board "Bienville Parish School Board"); the town has no private schools. Arcadia's two public schools are located in the Arcadia School Complex, which encompasses both [Arcadia High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia_High_School_(Louisiana) "Arcadia High School (Louisiana)") and Crawford Elementary School.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arcadia,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Transportation")]

The [Arcadia-Bienville Parish Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia-Bienville_Parish_Airport "Arcadia-Bienville Parish Airport") is located two nautical miles (2.3 mi; 3.7 km) southwest of Arcadia's central business district.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-21) The Bienville Parish Council on Aging provides public transit for the general population to locations within the town or close by, operating on an as-needed basis.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-22) Appointments should be made ahead of time. Private transport is also available for the area, including charter bus services such as J&T Charters, based in El Dorado, Arkansas.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia,_Louisiana#cite_note-23)

It has Calcasieu Office of Community Services and Calcasieu Voluntary Council in Aging; that's a COA? It is Calcasieu Voluntary Council in Aging, yes.

Also City of Shreveport? Not COA. City of Alexandria? Not COA. City of Monroe? Not COA.

Also City of Baton Rouge? not COA.

Camden Council on Aging? It's Cameron County? Cameron is a parish but the council is "Cameron Council on Aging, Inc" (city of Lake Charles). Lake Charles population ~49k >10k.

Also Desoto Council on Aging (Mansfield) – population ~7k? Mansfield 7k <10k (Wait population about 7,162? Actually 2020 population 7,162 for Mansfield? Let's check.

**Mansfield** is a small [city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City "City") in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [DeSoto Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeSoto_Parish,_Louisiana "DeSoto Parish, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) Mansfield is part of the [Shreveport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreveport,_Louisiana "Shreveport, Louisiana")–[Bossier City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bossier_City,_Louisiana "Bossier City, Louisiana")[metropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreveport-Bossier_City_metropolitan_area "Shreveport-Bossier City metropolitan area"), with a 2020 population of 4,714.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mansfield,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Mansfield had a population of 4,714. The median age was 38.2 years. 25.2% of residents were under the age of 18 and 17.9% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 83.6 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 76.8 males age 18 and over.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PL-8)

99.3% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.7% lived in rural areas.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DHC-9)

There were 1,857 households in Mansfield, of which 35.6% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 21.4% were married-couple households, 19.8% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 53.0% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 33.4% of all households were made up of individuals and 14.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-7)

There were 1,165 families residing in the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-7)

There were 2,153 housing units, of which 13.7% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.3% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.2%.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020DP-7)
